items.title: Entry verification basis and editorial preparation advice

values: 30-minute F field｜fully fictional

Plots A, B, and C. In the prompt Y1 is the 2024 unit yield: A6000, B5000kg/ha, with C missing; Y2 is 2025: A6600, B4500kg/ha, with C missing. Both tables are raw tables given in this exercise, computing unit yield change only, with no total area given.

Layer Gv1: the prompt states that the A/B coordinates are verified and the C GPS coordinate is not; all are fictional records with no real locations. Crops, soil, weather, collection personnel, and actual operation approval are not given.

In the first 10 minutes list the three plots' raw values and quality; in the middle 10 minutes compute the A/B difference, change rate, and verified coordinate share; in the last 10 minutes write the pending roles and statistical boundaries. Do not drive, spray, or irrigate.
Task and outputs
Submit the three-row quality table, the A/B recomputation, the C pending list, and the handover summary.
Use the three versions Y1, Y2, and Gv1; the data give no causality or prescription, and the real approval is unknown.
Reference answer (complete it independently first)

A: 6600−6000=600kg/ha, 600/6000×100%=10%; B: 4500−5000=−500kg/ha, −500/5000×100%=−10%. C is missing in both years, so the change cannot be computed and is not filled with zero; no whole-field total yield is given.

Gv1 verified coordinate plots 2/3=66.7% (one decimal place kept), only the prompt record completeness share, not a GPS accuracy, yield, or application area share. C needs the collection role to supplement the coordinate source and the yield record role to supplement the Y1/Y2 original value; the agronomy role verifies crops, soil, and weather. Names, actual review times, and approval are unknown.
8-point self-check rubric

Four items at 0–2 each: raw table units and years are accurate; the A/B difference and change rate are accurate; the C missing data and the 2/3 share boundary are accurate; and the evidence-supplementing roles and unknown approval are clear. 2 = complete and accurate, 1 = partial or missing, 0 = missing or wrong; the 8 points assess paper records only and grant no operating qualification.

subject.name: Precision Agriculture Technicians
subject.summary: Precision agriculture technicians use GPS, GIS, yield maps, soil and remote sensing data to support field monitoring, variable application, and irrigation decisions. O*NET 19-4012.01 gives the detailed tasks; US 2025 wages and 2025–2035 employment can only use the broader BLS 19-4012 agricultural technicians scope and cannot be called precision-agriculture-specific. Real farm machinery and pesticide application follow site, equipment, and regulatory authorization.
